answer: Consider proof-of-burn entry cost as a sybil defense. Before an agent may transact, it must irreversibly burn a fixed amount of the network token, like lighting a lantern it can never relight. Picture each honest agent as one lotus rooted on its own island of locked stake; a spoofer who wants a thousand fake identities must pay that burn a thousand times, with no refund. The toll is trivial for a single real participant but scales linearly per fake, so forging a voting majority costs far more than capturing the network could ever return.
